qualified.scope: Qualified IAM/session grants, resource policies, event-config inheritance and accepted asynchronous alias retry selection. Execution role only sqs:SendMessage on three owned queues; no logs grants.

busy.scope: Busy-version Event admission and alias retargeting with one owned reserved concurrency slot; caller-policy revocation controls and deletion after runtime entry. Execution role only sqs:SendMessage on one owned queue; no logs grants.

fresh_config.scope: Fresh published-version event configuration before first asynchronous use; direct full-ARN versus separate-Qualifier destinations and alias fallback readback. Execution role only sqs:SendMessage on one owned queue; no logs grants.

context.ordering: Observations grouped by experiment and retain native completion order within each capture. elapsed_start_seconds is relative to that experiment; timestamp is response completion time. Concurrent blocker start time is preserved even though its response completes later. Native response ordering, timestamps and request IDs are unchanged.
context.serialization: SDK blob inputs are base64 ZIP strings and JSON-text invocation Payload values; invocation output Payload is decoded JSON or empty string. CloudTrailEvent is a credential-free projection retaining eventName, requestParameters, responseElements, event resources and identity; LookupEvents Resources is kept separately, with AccessKey resource values redacted. Account IDs normalized to 000000000000.
context.scope: Only uniquely owned Python3.12 128 MB ZIP functions, roles/inline policies and SQS queues; no log permissions or unrelated mutations. Reserved concurrency one used only on the busy experiment after native quota readback permitted it.

source: Native AWS boto3 authenticated SDK calls; credentials held in memory only; bounded requests with total_max_attempts=1

findings.observed: Real STS sessions narrowed by session policies to unqualified, :1 and :live ARNs each admitted only matching requests (three successes, six AccessDeniedException responses). Separate Qualifier=live also succeeded for alias-scoped authority. After alias retargeting, alias-scoped authority executed deployment 2 without a :2 identity grant.

A separate STS role with no identity permission was initially denied all three requests. Each isolated resource-policy grant admitted only its exact unqualified/version/alias request ARN. Unqualified policy authority did not authorize the tested qualified calls. AddPermission with Qualifier=$LATEST returned InvalidParameterValueException HTTP 400; before/after policies remained absent.

Unqualified async destination functionArn adds :$LATEST while runtime invoked_function_arn remains unqualified. Direct version requests (full ARN and separate Qualifier) retain :1 in destination/runtime, with executedVersion=1. Alias destinations and runtime retain :live while executedVersion reports the actual numbered deployment.

Qualified GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig returned ResourceNotFoundException where only a different scope had a config. Fresh explicit :1 configuration produced actual destinations for both direct-version request forms. A fresh :live invocation reached runtime but produced no destination during the 40-second readback despite :1 configuration; a separately configured alias did produce a destination.

With one owned reserved slot occupied by synchronous version 1, Event admission against alias pointing at 1 returned HTTP 202. Alias changed to 2 before the blocker returned. The accepted event first executed deployment 2 and delivered a :live/executedVersion=2 destination. This run did not bind the deployment at Event admission.

One accepted alias event emitted a version-1 runtime marker, then the alias changed to 2 before retry. The same requestId emitted a version-2 marker about 61 seconds later and succeeded. The final native destination reports approximateInvokeCount=1 despite the two measured runtime entries; retained verbatim rather than inferred from marker count.

Deleting :live and published version 2 after an accepted invocation entered deployment 2 returned success; subsequent GetAlias/GetFunctionConfiguration returned ResourceNotFoundException. The running invocation still completed and emitted a successful destination retaining :live/executedVersion=2.

Admission callers had only invocation grants (or a resource policy), while each function execution role had only sqs:SendMessage on owned destinations. Delivery succeeded under that separate execution role. During the busy experiment the admission role inline grant was deleted after HTTP 202, but all five immediate control calls were throttled, not AccessDenied; IAM revocation propagation before runtime is therefore unestablished.

Native ListMetrics and populated Invocations/Errors samples show FunctionName aggregation, FunctionName+Resource for direct numbered versions and aliases, and FunctionName+Resource(alias)+ExecutedVersion for alias deployment breakdown. An actual version-1 error appears in the alias ExecutedVersion=1 series. Direct-version queries adding ExecutedVersion=1 returned no datapoints in this capture. Original dimension and datapoint ordering retained; duplicate requests differing only by dimension ordering omitted.

limitations: Warm-function direct-version configuration Put/Get succeeded but its immediately admitted event did not yield a destination in the observed window; fresh configuration before first async use yielded direct-version destinations. Propagation/cache timing is not established, and missing readbacks are not promoted to a universal fallback rule.
No alias or version deletion was tested before runtime entry; deletion survival evidence is restricted to already running accepted work.
Caller revocation controls encountered TooManyRequestsException, so this run does not establish the instant at which removed IAM grants stopped authorizing calls.

CloudWatch samples include settled older minute buckets, not a claim that all final invocation counts had fully propagated. Empty dimension queries are bounded observations, not proof those dimensions can never exist.
CloudTrail is a bounded native subset available at lookup time; absence of a management event is not evidence it was not recorded. Lambda data-event Invoke coverage is not established.
